newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops, rebels engaged in fierce battle.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops, rebels engaged in fierce battle.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops and Tamil Tiger rebels exchanged artillery fire on Thursday as fighting in the north of the island escalated, defence officials said.

Positions held by rebel fighters of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) in the mainly scrub Wanni region came under heavy attack when the army fired shells from bases at Welioya, Killinochichi and Elephant Pass in the north, officials said.
"The LTTE retailiated by shelling the Welioya camp, wounding three soldiers and killing one homeguard," one military official in the north said.
Other officials said nine members of the security forces had been killed and 45 wounded since the government launched its military offensive, codenamed "Jaya Sikuru" or "Sure of Victory", on Tuesday.
Unconfirmed reports from the north put the death toll at 19, including a few civilians.
"Yesterday there was severe confrontation. We hammered them hard and we expect high casualties on their side," military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga told Reuters.
Military officials said two army tanks were damaged in fighting on Wednesday after troops captured Omanthai town, along the strategic Jaffna-Vavuniya north-south highway.

The town fell after troops backed by helicopter gunships, artillery and tanks broke out of bases in Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, in a largely unopposed thrust into the rebel heartland.
Omanthai, a small agricultural community, constituted the southern forward defences of the LTTE, which controls vast swathes of land further north.

The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people gave died in the 13-year-old war, but the LTTE says the toll is higher.
Analysts said the aim of the offensive was to open a land supply route linking Vavuniya with the Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The clandestine Voice of Tiger radio, monitored in Vavuniya, said on Thursday that government troops had continued their assault and civilians were fleeing as the army advanced into the Wanni.
The radio said the LTTE had lost only two fighters in the first two days of the offensive. It did not say how many were wounded.

"Fighting continued late into Wednesday night and today there is heavy shelling from Welioya army positions," the radio said. It said Kfir air force jets had attacked the Mallavi and Puliyankulam areas.
"MI24 helicopters and tanks are smashing everything (along their path)," an LTTE statement said.
Aid workers in the north said at least 1,500 civilians living along the path of the army advance had left their homes and moved to safer areas near Madhu and Mannar in the northwest.
The main highway that links Sri Lanka's south with the war-ravaged north has been cut by the war.
But the LTTE's international spokesman in London, Anton Raja, told Reuters on Wednesday the rebels would fight to keep the road from falling into government hands.
"The LTTE will offer the toughest resistance to advancing armed forces," Raja said.
